     1→# BOS-ARSA Log
     2→
     3→**Amateurfunk Notfunkübung — Live-Erfassung, Multi-User, Auswertung**
     4→
     5→A real-time, multi-user web application for BOS-ARSA amateur radio exercises across Austria. Multiple operators simultaneously log signal reports from ~100 ham radio stations on repeaters and direct frequencies. BOS-ARSA Log replaces the shared Excel workbook and standalone HTML prototypes with a single unified tool.
     6→
     7→Part of the [oeradio.at](https://oeradio.at) ecosystem.
     8→
     9→## Tech Stack
    10→
    11→| Layer | Technology |
    12→|-------|-----------|
    13→| Frontend | React 18, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Socket.IO client |
    14→| Backend | Node.js, Express, TypeScript, Socket.IO server |
    15→| Database | SQLite via better-sqlite3 |
    16→| Auth | Username/password with bcrypt + JWT tokens |
    17→| Security | Helmet, rate limiting, CORS restriction, non-root Docker |
    18→| Deployment | Docker, Docker Compose, Cloudflare Tunnel |
    19→
    20→## Architecture
    21→
    22→```
    23→/client          React SPA (Vite)
    24→/server          Express API + WebSocket server
    25→/data            SQLite database (Docker volume-mounted)
    26→```
    27→
    28→- RESTful API for CRUD operations, WebSocket (Socket.IO) for real-time sync between concurrent users
    29→- Server serves the built client in production
    30→- SQLite keeps deployment simple — the data volume is small (~1,000 operators, ~200 reports/week)
    31→
    32→## Key Domain Concepts
    33→
    34→| Concept | Description |
    35→|---------|-------------|
    36→| **Operator (Rufzeichen)** | Ham radio callsign, e.g. OE8YML, S55UJE |
    37→| **Repeater/Umsetzer** | Radio relay station with TX frequency, offset, CTCSS |
    38→| **Linked Repeater** | One logical repeater spanning multiple physical sites (Einstiegspunkte) |
    39→| **Einstiegspunkt** | Physical entry point in a linked repeater network, e.g. Hermannskogel (HK) |
    40→| **Signal Report (Rapport)** | RST format, e.g. "5/9+30 HK" = R5 / S9+30dB via Hermannskogel |
    41→| **Exercise (Übung)** | One session with configured repeaters and collected reports |
    42→| **Bezirk** | Austrian political district, identified by 2-3 letter code |
    43→| **Bundesland** | Austrian state (OE1=Wien through OE9=Vorarlberg) |
    44→| **Nachbarland** | Neighbor country (SI, CZ, DE, IT, SK, HR, LI, CH, HU) |
    45→
    46→## Features
    47→
    48→### Dashboard
    49→
    50→- **Year filter** — Button row to switch between years (2026, 2027, ...), derived from existing data
    51→- **Type filter** — Checkbox filter by exercise type (KriKom, Notfunk, etc.), appears when multiple types exist in a year
    52→- Summary cards, trend chart, and exercise table filtered by selected year and type
    53→- Exercise table shows type (short label), name, participants, and reports with quarterly subtotals
    54→
    55→### Two Data Entry Modes
    56→
    57→- **Frequenzen (Land)** — Repeater-first entry. Select a repeater, enter reports grouped by Bezirk.
    58→- **OE-Link (Bund)** — Geography-first entry. Bundesland/Bezirk hierarchy with linked repeater selection per district. Reports stay in the Bundesland where they were entered, regardless of the repeater's physical location. Only available when OE-Link mode is enabled for the exercise.
    59→
    60→### Exercise Setup
    61→
    62→- **Exercise type** selection (Krisenkommunikationsübung, 80m Notfunk Runde, or custom free-text types)
    63→- Optional exercise name (e.g. "Sonntagsrunde KW 07")
    64→- Bundesland selection grid (OE1–OE9) with one-click activation of all repeaters per state
    65→- ~80 pre-configured Austrian repeaters from OEVSV data
    66→- Custom repeater and simplex frequency creation
    67→- OE-Link toggle for linked repeater mode
    68→- Per-repeater operator (OP) callsign assignment
    69→
    70→### Interactive Austria Map with Neighbor Countries
    71→
    72→- Choropleth map of Austria (OE1–OE9) with participant/report density
    73→- 9 neighbor countries displayed: Germany, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Hungary, Slovenia, Italy, Switzerland, Liechtenstein, Croatia
    74→- High-resolution borders from Natural Earth 10m data
    75→- Countries with participating operators are color-coded by activity level
    76→- Hover tooltips showing participant count and report count per region
    77→
    78→### Automatic Callsign-to-Country Assignment
    79→
    80→- Foreign callsign prefixes automatically mapped to the correct country (e.g. S55UJE → Slovenia, DL1ABC → Germany)
    81→- Supported prefixes: OE1–OE9, S5 (Slovenia), OK/OL (Czech Republic), DA-DR (Germany), I (Italy), OM (Slovakia), 9A (Croatia), HB0 (Liechtenstein), HB (Switzerland), HA/HG (Hungary)
    82→- Strips portable/mobile suffixes (/P, /M, /OE8) before matching
    83→- Auto-derived on operator creation; existing operators backfilled via migration
    84→
    85→### Live Multi-User
    86→
    87→- Socket.IO real-time sync — reports entered by one user appear instantly for all others
    88→- Running totals bar always visible: participant count, total reports, per-repeater counts
    89→- Optimized for speed: autofocus, enter-to-submit, auto-uppercase, keyboard shortcuts
    90→
    91→### Keyboard Shortcuts
    92→
    93→| Shortcut | Action |
    94→|----------|--------|
    95→| `Alt+1` through `Alt+9` | Insert "5/1" through "5/9" in rapport field |
    96→| `Ctrl+1` through `Ctrl+9` | Insert "OE1" through "OE9" in callsign field |
    97→| `Enter` | Submit report and clear fields |
    98→| `Arrow Up/Down` | Navigate autocomplete suggestions |
    99→| `Escape` | Close autocomplete dropdown |
   100→
   101→### Reports & Export
   102→
   103→- **Per-exercise reports** — Summary with per-repeater and per-Bezirk/Bundesland/Land breakdown
   104→- **Auswertung (Aggregated Reports)** — Date-range aggregated statistics across multiple exercises
   105→  - Quick-select buttons: Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4, full year
   106→  - Custom date range (Von / Bis) picker
   107→  - Exercise type filter (multi-select checkboxes: KriKom, Notfunk, etc.)
   108→  - Summary cards: unique participants, total reports, exercise count, average participants per exercise
   109→  - Collapsible exercise list with per-exercise breakdown
   110→  - Deduplicates participants across exercises for accurate totals
   111→- Interactive Austria map with neighbor countries showing participant distribution
   112→- Bar chart (stations vs. reports) and pie chart (distribution by Bundesland/Land)
   113→- Participants list with callsign, name, location, report count
   114→- Export formats:
   115→  - **PNG** — Full-page screenshot of the analytics view
   116→  - **ADIF** — Amateur Data Interchange Format (.adi) for import into QRZ.com, LOTW, and other logbook software
   117→  - **TXT OE-Link** — Bundesland-grouped text export
   118→  - **TXT Frequenzen** — Repeater-grouped text export
   119→  - **TXT Kombiniert** — Summary statistics with per-repeater breakdown
   120→
   121→### Bezirk Assignment
   122→
   123→- **Operator bezirk** (home location) and **report bezirk** (where the rapport was given) are independent
   124→- Operator home bezirk is auto-derived from QTH address when possible (matching against district names)
   125→- Report bezirk is stored per signal report from the entry row context
   126→- An operator can travel and report from any bezirk without affecting their registered home location
   127→- All stats, exports, and charts group by the report's bezirk
   128→
   129→### Operator Registry
   130→
   131→- Searchable operator database (callsign, name, QTH)
   132→- Quick-add during live entry when callsign not found
   133→- Inline editing of operator details (Name, QTH) directly from report entry forms
   134→- Operator Name and QTH displayed alongside callsign in all report lists
   135→- Paginated browsing (50 per page)
   136→- Bulk import from official Fernmeldebehörde Rufzeichenliste PDF (see below)
   137→
   138→### Security
   139→
   140→- Helmet security headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options)
   141→- Rate limiting on login (10 attempts per 15 minutes)
   142→- CORS restricted to configured origin
   143→- JWT secret fail-fast in production
   144→- Request body size limit (1MB)
   145→- Input length validation
   146→- Docker container runs as non-root user
   147→- Port bound to localhost only (Cloudflare tunnel access)
   148→
   149→### User Roles
   150→
   151→| Capability | Admin | Erfasser |
   152→|-----------|-------|----------|
   153→| Create exercises | ✓ | — |
   154→| Configure repeaters | ✓ | — |
   155→| Change exercise type/name/date | ✓ | — |
   156→| Enable OE-Link | ✓ | — |
   157→| Enter/edit/delete reports | ✓ | ✓ |
   158→| Manage operators | ✓ | ✓ |
   159→| View analytics & export | ✓ | ✓ |
   160→
   161→## Getting Started
   162→
   163→### Prerequisites
   164→
   165→- Node.js 20+
   166→- npm
   167→
   168→### Development
   169→
   170→```bash
   171→# Install dependencies
   172→npm install
   173→cd server && npm install && cd ..
   174→cd client && npm install && cd ..
   175→
   176→# Seed the database with reference data (idempotent — safe to run multiple times)
   177→npm run db:seed
   178→
   179→# Start both client and server in dev mode
   180→npm run dev
   181→```
   182→
   183→The client runs on `http://localhost:5173` with API proxy to `http://localhost:3000`.
   184→
   185→### Production (Docker)
   186→
   187→```bash
   188→# Build and run
   189→docker compose up -d
   190→
   191→# Seed database (first run only — idempotent, won't overwrite existing data)
   192→docker exec bosarsalog node dist/server/db/seed.js
   193→```
   194→
   195→Required environment variables:
   196→
   197→| Variable | Description |
   198→|----------|-------------|
   199→| `JWT_SECRET` | Random 64+ char secret (required in production) |
   200→| `CORS_ORIGIN` | Allowed origin URL (default: `https://bosarsalog.oeradio.at`) |
   201→| `DATABASE_PATH` | SQLite DB path (default: `/data/bosarsalog.db`) |
   202→
   203→## API
   204→
   205→All endpoints are prefixed with `/api/v1/`. Protected routes require `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
   206→
   207→### Auth
   208→
   209→```
   210→POST /api/v1/auth/login    { username, password } -> { token, admin }
   211→```
   212→
   213→### Exercises
   214→
   215→```
   216→GET    /api/v1/exercises              List all (with summary stats)
   217→POST   /api/v1/exercises              Create { date, name, exercise_type }
   218→GET    /api/v1/exercises/:id          Full exercise with reports
   219→PATCH  /api/v1/exercises/:id          Update (name, exercise_type, organisator, oe_link)
   220→GET    /api/v1/exercises/:id/stats    Live statistics
   221→GET    /api/v1/exercises/:id/reports  All signal reports
   222→POST   /api/v1/exercises/:id/reports  Create report
   223→PATCH  /api/v1/exercises/:id/reports/:rid  Edit report
   224→DELETE /api/v1/exercises/:id/reports/:rid  Delete report
   225→```
   226→
   227→### Exercise Repeaters
   228→
   229→```
   230→GET    /api/v1/exercises/:id/repeaters
   231→POST   /api/v1/exercises/:id/repeaters      Activate repeater
   232→PATCH  /api/v1/exercises/:id/repeaters/:rid  Update OP assignment
   233→DELETE /api/v1/exercises/:id/repeaters/:rid  Deactivate repeater
   234→```
   235→
   236→### Operators
   237→
   238→```
   239→GET    /api/v1/operators         List/search (?q= for autocomplete)
   240→POST   /api/v1/operators         Quick-add new operator
   241→GET    /api/v1/operators/:id     Full profile with history
   242→PATCH  /api/v1/operators/:id     Update operator
   243→```
   244→
   245→### Reference Data
   246→
   247→```
   248→GET /api/v1/reference/bundeslaender
   249→GET /api/v1/reference/bezirke
   250→GET /api/v1/reference/einstiegspunkte
   251→GET /api/v1/repeaters
   252→GET /api/v1/repeaters/:id/einstiegspunkte
   253→```
   254→
   255→### Aggregated Reports
   256→
   257→```
   258→GET /api/v1/reports/stats?from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD[&types=...]   Aggregated stats (optional type filter)
   259→```
   260→
   261→### Export
   262→
   263→```
   264→GET /api/v1/export/exercises/:id/bund      TXT (Bundesland-grouped)
   265→GET /api/v1/export/exercises/:id/land      TXT (Repeater-grouped)
   266→GET /api/v1/export/exercises/:id/combined  Summary report
   267→```
   268→
   269→### WebSocket Events (Socket.IO)
   270→
   271→```
   272→Client -> Server:
   273→  join_exercise      { exercise_id }
   274→  leave_exercise     { exercise_id }
   275→  report_created     { report data }
   276→  report_updated     { report data }
   277→  report_deleted     { report_id }
   278→  attendance_updated { attendance data }
   279→
   280→Server -> Client (broadcast):
   281→  report_created     { report, entered_by }
   282→  report_updated     { report, entered_by }
   283→  report_deleted     { report_id, entered_by }
   284→  attendance_updated { attendance, entered_by }
   285→```
   286→
   287→## Rufzeichen Import (Fernmeldebehörde PDF)
   288→
   289→Import operators from the official Austrian Rufzeichenliste PDF published by the Fernmeldebüro:
   290→
   291→```bash
   292→# Update mode (default) — insert new, update existing name/qth
   293→RUFZEICHEN_MODE=update npm run import:rufzeichen -- /path/to/Rufzeichenliste.pdf
   294→
   295→# Skip mode — insert new only, leave existing untouched
   296→RUFZEICHEN_MODE=skip npm run import:rufzeichen -- /path/to/Rufzeichenliste.pdf
   297→```
   298→
   299→Requires `pdftotext` (poppler-utils). On NixOS: `nix-shell -p nodejs poppler-utils --run "..."`.
   300→
   301→The script parses callsign, name, and Standort (QTH) from the PDF table. Bundesland is auto-derived from the callsign prefix. Redacted entries (`*-*-*`) are skipped. The import is idempotent.
   302→
   303→## Seed Data
   304→
   305→The seed script (`npm run db:seed`) is **idempotent** — it only inserts data if the tables are empty, and never deletes existing data. It populates:
   306→
   307→- **18 Bundesländer** — 9 Austrian states + 9 international entries
   308→- **84 Bezirke** — Austrian political districts with capital flags
   309→- **~80 Repeaters** — Comprehensive OEVSV data across OE1–OE9 plus international and simplex
   310→- **12 Einstiegspunkte** — Entry points for the Magdalensberg linked system
   311→- **2 Users** — Admin and operator accounts
   312→
   313→## Conventions
   314→
   315→- German UI text, English code
   316→- Callsigns always uppercase
   317→- RST format: R/S with optional +dB modifier and location suffix
   318→- All timestamps in Europe/Vienna timezone
   319→- API prefix: `/api/v1/`
   320→- Bezirk badges: Hauptstadt = red, normal = gray
   321→- Bundesland headers with blue badges
   322→
   323→## License
   324→
   325→MIT

   262→                <th className="text-left px-3 py-2 border-b font-semibold">Format</th>
   263→                <th className="text-left px-3 py-2 border-b font-semibold">Beschreibung</th>
   264→              </tr>
   265→            </thead>
   266→            <tbody>
   267→              <Shortcut keys="PNG Auswertung" desc="Screenshot der gesamten Auswertungsseite" />
   268→              <Shortcut keys="ADIF (.adi)" desc="QSO-Daten für QRZ.com, LOTW und andere Logbuch-Software" />
   269→              <Shortcut keys="TXT — OE-Link" desc="Textdatei, gruppiert nach Bundesland und Bezirk" />
   270→              <Shortcut keys="TXT — Frequenzen" desc="Textdatei, gruppiert nach Umsetzer und Bezirk" />
   271→              <Shortcut keys="TXT — Kombiniert" desc="Zusammenfassung mit Statistiken und Umsetzer-Aufschlüsselung" />
   272→            </tbody>
   273→          </table>
   274→        </div>
   275→      </Section>
   276→
   277→      {/* ── Rufzeichen-Verwaltung ── */}
   278→      <Section title="7. Rufzeichen-Verwaltung">
   279→        <p>
   280→          Unter <b>Rufzeichen</b> in der Navigation finden Sie die Operator-Datenbank.
   281→        </p>
   282→        <h4 className="font-semibold text-[#1e3a5f] mt-3">Suche</h4>
   283→        <p>
   284→          Das Suchfeld durchsucht Rufzeichen, Name und QTH gleichzeitig. Die Suche startet automatisch
   285→          nach kurzer Verzögerung (300ms).
   286→        </p>
   287→        <h4 className="font-semibold text-[#1e3a5f] mt-3">Neuen Operator anlegen</h4>
   288→        <p>
   289→          Mit <b>+ Neu</b> können Sie manuell einen neuen Operator anlegen (Rufzeichen, Name, QTH, Bezirk, Bundesland).
   290→          Operatoren werden auch automatisch angelegt, wenn ein unbekanntes Rufzeichen bei der Datenerfassung eingegeben wird.
   291→        </p>
   292→        <h4 className="font-semibold text-[#1e3a5f] mt-3">Automatische Länderzuordnung</h4>
   293→        <p>
   294→          Das Bundesland bzw. Nachbarland wird automatisch anhand des Rufzeichen-Präfixes zugeordnet
   295→          (z.B. OE8 → Kärnten, S55 → Slowenien, DL → Deutschland).
   296→          Suffixe wie /P, /M oder /OE8 werden dabei ignoriert.
   297→        </p>
   298→        <h4 className="font-semibold text-[#1e3a5f] mt-3">Automatische Bezirkszuordnung</h4>
   299→        <p>
   300→          Der <b>Bezirk</b> (Heimatbezirk) wird nach Möglichkeit automatisch aus dem QTH (Standort) abgeleitet
   301→          (z.B. „Graz" → GC, „Wien" → WC, „Mödling" → MD). Wenn keine Zuordnung möglich ist,
   302→          kann der Bezirk manuell gesetzt werden.
   303→        </p>
   304→        <h4 className="font-semibold text-[#1e3a5f] mt-3">Bezirk in Rapports vs. Rufzeichenliste</h4>
   305→        <p>
   306→          Der <b>Heimatbezirk</b> eines Operators (in der Rufzeichenliste) und der <b>Rapport-Bezirk</b> (wo der Rapport
   307→          abgegeben wurde) sind unabhängig voneinander. Ein Operator kann reisen und von jedem Bezirk aus
   308→          einen Rapport abgeben, ohne dass sein Heimatbezirk verändert wird.
   309→          Auswertungen, Exporte und Diagramme gruppieren nach dem Rapport-Bezirk.
   310→        </p>
   311→        <h4 className="font-semibold text-[#1e3a5f] mt-3">Operator bearbeiten</h4>
   312→        <p>
   313→          Klicken Sie auf <b>Bearb.</b> in der Operatoren-Tabelle, um alle Felder inline zu bearbeiten.
   314→          Bestätigen Sie mit dem Häkchen oder brechen Sie mit X ab.
   315→        </p>
   316→      </Section>
   317→
   318→      {/* ── Rufzeichen-Import ── */}
   319→      <Section title="8. Rufzeichen-Import (Fernmeldebehörde)">
   320→        <p>
   321→          Rufzeichen können aus der offiziellen <b>Rufzeichenliste der Fernmeldebehörde</b> (PDF) automatisch
   322→          importiert werden. Das Skript liest die PDF-Datei, extrahiert Rufzeichen, Name und Standort (QTH)
   323→          und aktualisiert die Operator-Datenbank.
   324→        </p>
   325→        <h4 className="font-semibold text-[#1e3a5f] mt-3">Importmodus</h4>
   326→        <ul className="list-disc ml-5 space-y-1">
   327→          <li><b>RUFZEICHEN_MODE=update</b> — Neue Rufzeichen einfügen, bestehende mit Name/QTH aktualisieren (Standard)</li>
   328→          <li><b>RUFZEICHEN_MODE=skip</b> — Nur neue Rufzeichen einfügen, bestehende nicht verändern</li>
   329→        </ul>
   330→        <h4 className="font-semibold text-[#1e3a5f] mt-3">Ausführung</h4>
   331→        <p>
   332→          Das Bundesland wird automatisch aus dem Rufzeichen-Präfix abgeleitet (OE1 = Wien, OE8 = Kärnten, usw.).
   333→          Gesperrte Rufzeichen (<code>*-*-*</code>) werden übersprungen.
   334→          Der Import ist idempotent — bei unverändertem Datenbestand werden keine Änderungen vorgenommen.
   335→        </p>
   336→        <p>
   337→          Voraussetzung: <code>pdftotext</code> (poppler-utils) muss installiert sein.
   338→        </p>
   339→      </Section>
   340→
   341→      {/* ── Rollen ── */}
   342→      <Section title="9. Benutzerrollen">
   343→        <div className="overflow-x-auto">
   344→          <table className="w-full text-sm border border-gray-200 mt-2">
   345→            <thead className="bg-gray-50">
   346→              <tr>
   347→                <th className="text-left px-3 py-2 border-b font-semibold">Funktion</th>
   348→                <th className="text-center px-3 py-2 border-b font-semibold">Admin</th>
   349→                <th className="text-center px-3 py-2 border-b font-semibold">Erfasser</th>
   350→              </tr>
   351→            </thead>
   352→            <tbody className="divide-y divide-gray-100">
   353→              <RoleRow label="Übung erstellen" admin operator={false} />
   354→              <RoleRow label="Übungstyp/Name/Datum ändern" admin operator={false} />
   355→              <RoleRow label="Umsetzer konfigurieren" admin operator={false} />
   356→              <RoleRow label="OE-Link aktivieren" admin operator={false} />
   357→              <RoleRow label="Bundesländer aktivieren" admin operator={false} />
   358→              <RoleRow label="Rapporte erfassen" admin operator />
   359→              <RoleRow label="Rapporte bearbeiten/löschen" admin operator />
   360→              <RoleRow label="Operatoren verwalten" admin operator />
   361→              <RoleRow label="Auswertung ansehen" admin operator />
   362→              <RoleRow label="Daten exportieren" admin operator />
   363→            </tbody>
   364→          </table>
   365→        </div>
   366→      </Section>
   367→
   368→      {/* ── Tipps ── */}
   369→      <Section title="10. Tipps für die Praxis">
   370→        <ul className="list-disc ml-5 space-y-2">
   371→          <li>
   372→            <b>Vor der Übung:</b> Admin erstellt die Übung, wählt die Bundesländer und aktiviert die benötigten Umsetzer.
   373→            OP-Rufzeichen pro Umsetzer eintragen.
   374→          </li>
   375→          <li>
   376→            <b>Während der Übung:</b> Alle Erfasser melden sich an und öffnen die Übung.
   377→            Rapporte werden live synchronisiert — jeder sieht sofort, was die anderen eingeben.
   378→          </li>
   379→          <li>
   380→            <b>Schnelle Eingabe:</b> Nutzen Sie Alt+1-9 für schnelle RST-Eingabe und Strg+1-9 für OE-Präfixe.
   381→            Nach Enter springt der Fokus automatisch zum nächsten Rufzeichen-Feld.
   382→          </li>
   383→          <li>
   384→            <b>Unbekannte Rufzeichen:</b> Wenn ein Rufzeichen nicht in der Datenbank ist, wird es beim Speichern
   385→            automatisch als neuer Operator angelegt.
   386→          </li>
   387→          <li>
   388→            <b>Nach der Übung:</b> Auf der Auswertungsseite können Diagramme und Textdateien exportiert werden.
   389→          </li>
   390→        </ul>
   391→      </Section>
   392→
   393→      <div className="text-xs text-gray-400 pt-4 border-t">
   394→        BOS-ARSA Log &mdash; Im Sinne der Sicherheit
   395→      </div>
   396→    </div>
   397→  );
   398→}

   400→function Section({ title, children }: { title: string; children: React.ReactNode }) {
   401→  return (
   402→    <section className="space-y-2">
   403→      <h2 className="text-base font-bold text-[#1e3a5f] border-b border-gray-200 pb-1">{title}</h2>
   404→      <div className="text-sm text-gray-700 space-y-2">{children}</div>
   405→    </section>
   406→  );
   407→}
   408→
   409→function Shortcut({ keys, desc }: { keys: string; desc: string }) {
   410→  return (
   411→    <tr className="border-b border-gray-100">
   412→      <td className="px-3 py-1.5 font-mono text-xs whitespace-nowrap">{keys}</td>
   413→      <td className="px-3 py-1.5">{desc}</td>
   414→    </tr>
   415→  );
   416→}
   417→
   418→function RoleRow({ label, admin, operator }: { label: string; admin: boolean; operator: boolean }) {
   419→  return (
   420→    <tr>
   421→      <td className="px-3 py-1.5">{label}</td>
   422→      <td className="px-3 py-1.5 text-center">{admin ? '✓' : '—'}</td>
   423→      <td className="px-3 py-1.5 text-center">{operator ? '✓' : '—'}</td>
   424→    </tr>
   425→  );
   426→}

Based on my reading of the ExerciseSetupPage.tsx file, here's how repeaters are currently displayed:

## Key Finding: Linked Repeaters Are Mixed Together

**Linked repeaters (with `is_linked=1`) are NOT separated from regular repeaters.** They are displayed together in the same Bundesland sections, distinguished only by a visual badge.

### Relevant Code Sections:

**Line 56-57: Repeater filtering by Bundesland**
```typescript
const repeatersForBl = (blCode: string) =>
  allRepeaters.filter(r => r.bundesland_code === blCode && r.type !== 'simplex');
```
This filter only excludes simplex frequencies, not linked repeaters. All repeaters (linked or not) for a Bundesland are grouped together.

**Line 315-338: Per-Bundesland repeater display**
```typescript
{blRepeaters.map(rep => {
  const active = activeRepeaters.find(r => r.repeater_id === rep.id);
  return (
    <div key={rep.id} className="flex items-center gap-3 py-2 border-b border-gray-100">
      <label className={`flex items-center gap-1.5 sm:gap-2 flex-1 flex-wrap ...`}>
        <input type="checkbox" checked={!!active} ... />
        <span className="font-medium text-xs sm:text-sm">{rep.short_name}</span>
        <span className="text-xs text-gray-500 hidden sm:inline">
          {rep.frequency_mhz && `${rep.frequency_mhz} MHz`}
          {rep.callsign && ` (${rep.callsign})`}
        </span>
        {rep.ctcss_hz && <span className="text-xs text-gray-400 hidden md:inline">CTCSS {rep.ctcss_hz}</span>}
        {rep.is_linked ? <span className="text-xs bg-blue-100 text-blue-700 px-1.5 py-0.5 rounded">oelink</span> : null}
        {rep.is_custom ? <span className="text-xs bg-purple-100 text-purple-700 px-1.5 py-0.5 rounded">custom</span> : null}
      </label>
    </div>
  );
})}
```

**Key observation (Line 333):** Linked repeaters are visually distinguished with a **blue badge** labeled "oelink", but they're mixed in the same list as regular repeaters. There is **no separate filtering or grouping by `is_linked`** — it's purely a UI badge indicator.

## Summary

The UI approach is **mixing-together**: All repeaters for a Bundesland are shown in one section, with linked repeaters only differentiated by a blue "oelink" badge at the end of the repeater line. They are not separated into distinct sections or lists.

> AGENT

Problems found:

**Wrong `is_capital` (Statutarstädte, not Landeshauptstädte):**
- KS (Krems) — not the capital of NÖ
- SE (Steyr) — not the capital of OÖ
- WE (Wels) — not the capital of OÖ
- VI (Villach) — not the capital of Kärnten

**Missing Landeshauptstädte:**
- EC — Eisenstadt (Burgenland)
- LC — Linz (OÖ)
- GC — Graz (Steiermark)
- IC — Innsbruck (Tirol)

**Missing Bezirke:**
- WY — Waidhofen/Ybbs (NÖ)
- KB — Kitzbühel (Tirol)
- LA — Landeck (Tirol)
- BZ — Bludenz (Vorarlberg)

Let me fix all at once — production DB and seed.ts.

Based on my web search results, I can provide you with information about Austrian political districts (Bezirke) and their KFZ codes:

## Overview

As of 2025, there are 79 political districts (politische Bezirke) in Austria, with additional statutory cities that also function as administrative units. The core registration code consists of one or two letters indicating the issuing district (e.g., "W" for Vienna).

## Structure of Austrian Districts

In the provincial laws of Lower Austria and Vorarlberg, districts headed by district commissions are called administrative districts (Verwaltungsbezirke). In Burgenland, Carinthia, Salzburg, Styria, Upper Austria, and Tyrol, the term used is political district (politischer Bezirk).

## Vehicle Registration System

The first one or two letters on vehicle registration plates are abbreviations for the respective registration district, and all abbreviations and their corresponding registration districts have been compiled in lists.

## Finding Complete Lists

While my search found references to comprehensive lists of KFZ codes organized by federal state (Bundesland), the complete detailed list with all individual district codes would be best found at:
- Sources like oesterreich.gv.at provide comprehensive lists with all license plate abbreviations for each district in the federal state, sorted by Bundesland and listing the respective registration authority
- The Cactus2000 website allows viewing Austrian license plates with the ability to filter by individual federal state

For the most current and complete 2025 listing of all Austrian Bezirke with their KFZ Kennzeichen codes organized by federal state, the official Austrian government portal (oesterreich.gv.at) would provide the authoritative source.

## COMPREHENSIVE FINDINGS - BundMode Report Creation Issue

### Problem Summary
Reports created in BundMode (OE-Link) for exercise `e0178522-bc83-4cbf-a502-1a93bd5744b1` are not appearing or not being created. The root cause is a database schema mismatch.

### Key Findings

#### 1. **Database Schema Missing `bezirk_code` Column** (/home/achildrenmile/bosarsalog/data/bosarsalog.db)
   - **signal_reports table:** Missing `bezirk_code` TEXT column
   - Current columns: id, exercise_id, operator_id, repeater_id, readability, strength, db_over_s9, einstiegspunkt_id, is_op_marker, notes, entered_by, created_at, updated_at
   - **Missing columns:**
     - `bezirk_code` TEXT (required by BundMode filtering and report creation)

#### 2. **repeaters Table Missing Columns** (/home/achildrenmile/bosarsalog/data/bosarsalog.db)
   - **Missing:** `bundesland_code` TEXT and `is_custom` INTEGER columns

#### 3. **exercises Table Has Wrong Schema**
   - **Current:** INTEGER id, status TEXT column

   - The code was updated to use TEXT UUIDs (see git history: "GUID exercises + status removal") but the database wasn't migrated

   342→interface BezirkRowProps {

   357→function BezirkRow({ bezirk, reports, linkedRepeaters, defaultRepeaterId, onSubmit, onEdit, onDelete, editingId, editForm, onEditChange, onEditSave, onEditCancel }: BezirkRowProps) {
   358→  const [form, setForm] = useState<EntryForm>({ callsign: '', operator: null, rapport: '5/9', notes: '', opName: '', opQth: '' });
   359→  const [repeaterId, setRepeaterId] = useState(defaultRepeaterId);
   360→  const callsignRef = useRef<CallsignInputRef>(null);
   361→  const rapportRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null);
   362→
   363→  useEffect(() => {
   364→    if (defaultRepeaterId && !repeaterId) setRepeaterId(defaultRepeaterId);
   365→  }, [defaultRepeaterId]);
   366→
   367→  const handleSubmit = (e: FormEvent) => {
   368→    e.preventDefault();
   369→    if (!form.callsign && !form.operator) return;
   370→    if (!repeaterId) return;
   371→    onSubmit(repeaterId, form);
   372→    setForm({ callsign: '', operator: null, rapport: '5/9', notes: '', opName: '', opQth: '' });
   373→    setTimeout(() => callsignRef.current?.focus(), 50);
   374→  };
   375→
   376→  const saveOperatorField = (field: 'name' | 'qth', value: string) => {
   377→    if (!form.operator?.id) return;
   378→    const original = field === 'name' ? (form.operator.name || '') : (form.operator.qth || '');
   379→    if (value === original) return;
   380→    apiFetch(`/api/v1/operators/${form.operator.id}`, {
   381→      method: 'PATCH',
   382→      body: JSON.stringify({ [field]: value || null }),
   383→    }).then(() => {
   384→      setForm(f => ({ ...f, operator: { ...f.operator, [field]: value || null } }));
   385→    }).catch(() => {});
   386→  };
   387→
   388→  return (
   389→    <div className="px-2 sm:px-3 py-1.5">
   390→      <div className="flex items-center gap-1.5 sm:gap-2 mb-1">
   391→        <span className={`text-xs font-mono px-1.5 py-0.5 rounded text-white ${bezirk.code === '??' ? 'bg-[#ffc107] text-gray-800' : bezirk.is_capital ? 'bg-[#dc3545]' : 'bg-[#6c757d]'}`}>
   392→          {bezirk.code === '??' ? '??' : bezirk.code}
   393→        </span>
   394→        <span className="text-xs text-gray-500 truncate">{bezirk.name}</span>
   395→        {reports.length > 0 && <span className="text-xs text-gray-400 flex-shrink-0">({reports.length})</span>}
   396→      </div>
   397→
   398→      {reports.length > 0 && (
   399→        <table className="w-full text-xs mb-1">
   400→          <tbody>

   405→                    <div className="flex items-center gap-1 bg-blue-50 rounded p-1 flex-wrap" onKeyDown={e => { if (e.key === 'Enter') { e.preventDefault(); onEditSave(); } }}>
   406→                      <span className="font-mono font-medium">{r.callsign}</span>
   407→                      <input value={editForm.opName} onChange={e => onEditChange({ ...editForm, opName: e.target.value })} placeholder="Name" className="border rounded px-1 py-0.5 text-xs w-16 sm:w-20 hidden sm:block" />
   408→                      <input value={editForm.opQth} onChange={e => onEditChange({ ...editForm, opQth: e.target.value })} placeholder="QTH" className="border rounded px-1 py-0.5 text-xs w-14 sm:w-16 hidden sm:block" />
   409→                      <input value={editForm.rapport} onChange={e => onEditChange({ ...editForm, rapport: e.target.value.toUpperCase() })} className="border rounded px-1 py-0.5 font-mono text-xs w-16 sm:w-20" autoFocus />
   410→                      <input value={editForm.notes} onChange={e => onEditChange({ ...editForm, notes: e.target.value })} placeholder="Sonst." className="border rounded px-1 py-0.5 text-xs w-16 sm:w-20" />
   411→                      <button onClick={onEditSave} className="text-green-600 text-xs font-bold">OK</button>
   412→                      <button onClick={onEditCancel} className="text-gray-400 text-xs">X</button>
   413→                    </div>

   415→                ) : (

   422→                    </td>
   423→                    <td className="py-0.5 text-blue-600 text-xs cursor-pointer hidden sm:table-cell" onClick={() => onEdit(r)}>{r.repeater_name || ''}</td>
   424→                    <td className="py-0.5 font-mono text-gray-500 w-16 sm:w-24 cursor-pointer" onClick={() => onEdit(r)}>
   425→                      {r.readability && r.strength ? `${r.readability}/${r.strength}${r.db_over_s9 || ''}` : '—'}
   426→                    </td>
   427→                    <td className="py-0.5 text-gray-500 cursor-pointer hidden sm:table-cell" onClick={() => onEdit(r)}>{r.notes || ''}</td>
   428→                    <td className="py-0.5 w-4">
   429→                      <button onClick={() => onDelete(r.id)} className="text-red-400 hover:text-red-600 opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100">x</button>
   430→                    </td>
   431→                  </>
   432→                )}
   433→              </tr>
   434→            ))}
   435→          </tbody>
   436→        </table>

   438→
   439→      <form onSubmit={handleSubmit} className="flex items-center gap-1">

   445→          >
   446→            {linkedRepeaters.map(r => (
   447→              <option key={r.id} value={r.id}>
   448→                {r.site_name || r.short_name}{r.callsign ? ` (${r.callsign})` : ''}
   449→              </option>
   450→            ))}
   451→          </select>
   452→        )}
   453→        <CallsignInput
   454→          ref={callsignRef}

   457→          onSelect={op => {
   458→            setForm(f => ({ ...f, operator: op, callsign: op.callsign, opName: op.name || '', opQth: op.qth || '' }));
   459→            setTimeout(() => { const el = rapportRef.current; if (el) { el.focus(); el.setSelectionRange(el.value.length, el.value.length); } }, 50);
   460→          }}
   461→          onEnter={() => setTimeout(() => { const el = rapportRef.current; if (el) { el.focus(); el.setSelectionRange(el.value.length, el.value.length); } }, 50)}
   462→          className="w-24 sm:w-28"
   463→        />
   464→        <input
   465→          type="text"
   466→          value={form.opName}
   467→          onChange={e => setForm(f => ({ ...f, opName: e.target.value }))}
   468→          onBlur={e => saveOperatorField('name', e.target.value)}
   469→          placeholder="Name"
   470→          className="border border-gray-300 rounded px-1.5 py-0.5 text-xs w-20 sm:w-24 focus:outline-none focus:ring-1 focus:ring-blue-500 hidden sm:block"
   471→        />
   472→        <input
   473→          type="text"
   474→          value={form.opQth}
   475→          onChange={e => setForm(f => ({ ...f, opQth: e.target.value }))}
   476→          onBlur={e => saveOperatorField('qth', e.target.value)}
   477→          placeholder="QTH"
   478→          className="border border-gray-300 rounded px-1.5 py-0.5 text-xs w-16 sm:w-20 focus:outline-none focus:ring-1 focus:ring-blue-500 hidden sm:block"
   479→        />
   480→        <input
   481→          ref={rapportRef}
   482→          type="text"
   483→          value={form.rapport}
   484→          onChange={e => setForm(f => ({ ...f, rapport: e.target.value.toUpperCase() }))}
   485→          placeholder="5/9"
   486→          className="border border-gray-300 rounded px-1.5 py-0.5 font-mono text-xs w-16 sm:w-20 focus:outline-none focus:ring-1 focus:ring-blue-500"
   487→          onKeyDown={e => {
   488→            if (e.altKey && e.key >= '1' && e.key <= '9') {
   489→              e.preventDefault();
   490→              setForm(f => ({ ...f, rapport: `5/${e.key}` }));

   492→          }}
   493→        />
   494→        <input
   495→          type="text"
   496→          value={form.notes}
   497→          onChange={e => setForm(f => ({ ...f, notes: e.target.value }))}
   498→          placeholder="Sonst."
   499→          className="border border-gray-300 rounded px-1.5 py-0.5 text-xs flex-1 min-w-[40px] sm:min-w-[60px] focus:outline-none focus:ring-1 focus:ring-blue-500"
   500→        />
   501→        <button type="submit" title="Rapport speichern (Enter)" className="bg-[#c8102e] hover:bg-[#a00d24] text-white px-2 py-0.5 rounded text-xs flex-shrink-0">
   502→          + ↵
   503→        </button>

   101→  if (!exercise) return <p className="text-red-500 p-4">Übung nicht gefunden</p>;
   102→
   103→  return (
   104→    <div className="space-y-4">
   105→      <div className="flex items-center justify-between flex-wrap gap-2">
   106→        <h1 className="text-base sm:text-xl font-bold text-[#1e3a5f] min-w-0">
   107→          <span className="block sm:inline">{exercise.name || 'Übung'}</span>
   108→          <span className="hidden sm:inline"> — </span>
   109→          <span className="block sm:inline text-sm sm:text-xl">{new Date(exercise.date + 'T00:00:00').toLocaleDateString('de-AT', { day: '2-digit', month: '2-digit', year: 'numeric' })}</span>
   110→        </h1>
   111→        <div className="flex items-center gap-2 flex-wrap">
   112→          <div className="flex items-center gap-1.5">
   113→            <label className={`text-xs ${organisator ? 'text-gray-500' : 'text-[#c8102e] font-semibold'}`}>Organisator:</label>
   114→            <input
   115→              type="text"
   116→              value={organisator}
   117→              onChange={e => setOrganisator(e.target.value.toUpperCase())}
   118→              onBlur={e => updateOrganisator(e.target.value.toUpperCase())}
   119→              placeholder="Rufzeichen"
   120→              className={`border rounded px-2 py-1 text-sm font-mono uppercase w-24 sm:w-28 focus:outline-none focus:ring-2 focus:ring-blue-500 ${organisator ? 'border-gray-300' : 'border-[#c8102e] placeholder-[#c8102e]/60'}`}
   121→            />
   122→          </div>
   123→          <Link to={`/exercises/${id}/setup`} className="bg-gray-200 hover:bg-gray-300 text-gray-700 px-2 sm:px-3 py-1 rounded text-xs sm:text-sm">
   124→            Einrichten
   125→          </Link>
   126→          <Link to={`/exercises/${id}/reports`} className="bg-red-100 hover:bg-red-200 text-red-800 px-2 sm:px-3 py-1 rounded text-xs sm:text-sm">
   127→            Auswertung
   128→          </Link>
   129→        </div>
   130→      </div>
   131→
   132→      <RunningTotals stats={stats} />
   133→
   134→      {oeLinkEnabled && (
   135→        <div className="flex gap-1 bg-white rounded-lg p-1 shadow-sm w-full sm:w-fit">
   136→          <button
   137→            onClick={() => setMode('land')}
   138→            className={`flex-1 sm:flex-none px-3 sm:px-4 py-1.5 rounded text-xs sm:text-sm font-medium ${mode === 'land' ? 'bg-[#1e3a5f] text-white' : 'text-gray-600 hover:bg-gray-100'}`}
   139→          >
   140→            Frequenzen
   141→          </button>
   142→          <button
   143→            onClick={() => setMode('bund')}
   144→            className={`flex-1 sm:flex-none px-3 sm:px-4 py-1.5 rounded text-xs sm:text-sm font-medium ${mode === 'bund' ? 'bg-[#1e3a5f] text-white' : 'text-gray-600 hover:bg-gray-100'}`}
   145→          >
   146→            OE-Link
   147→          </button>
   148→        </div>
   149→      )}
   150→
   151→      {mode === 'land' || !oeLinkEnabled ? (
   152→        <LandMode
   153→          exerciseId={id!}
   154→          repeaters={exercise.repeaters || []}
   155→          reports={reports}
   156→          onReportCreated={handleReportCreated}
   157→          onReportUpdated={handleReportUpdated}
   158→          onReportDeleted={handleReportDeleted}
   159→        />
   160→      ) : (
   161→        <BundMode
   162→          exerciseId={id!}
   163→          reports={reports}
   164→          onReportCreated={handleReportCreated}
   165→          onReportUpdated={handleReportUpdated}
   166→          onReportDeleted={handleReportDeleted}
   167→        />
   168→      )}
   169→    </div>
   170→  );
   171→}

> AGENT

Found the bugs. There are two issues:

1. **BundMode filter is too strict** (line 216): `reports.filter(r => r.bezirk_code && blBezirkCodes.has(r.bezirk_code) && r.repeater_is_linked)` — reports with `null` bezirk_code are invisible. All 14 Hermannskogel reports have `bezirk_code: null`, so they never appear.

2. **PATCH doesn't update bezirk_code**: When re-entering an operator that already has a report (UNIQUE constraint), the update doesn't set bezirk_code, so it stays null.

Let me fix both.

> TOOL

tool_use Edit
id: toolu_018ZjrTHEZmUUaoNv2iqTWkh
```json
{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/home/achildrenmile/bosarsalog/client/src/components/BundMode.tsx",
  "old_string": "  return (\n    <div className=\"space-y-2\">\n      {bundeslaender.filter(bl => !bl.is_international).map(bl => {\n        const blBezirke = bezirke.filter(b => b.bundesland_code === bl.code);\n        const defaultRepId = blRepSelection[bl.code] || 0;\n        // Match reports by bezirk's Bundesland, only for linked repeaters\n        const blBezirkCodes = new Set(blBezirke.map(b => b.code));\n        const blReports = reports.filter(r => r.bezirk_code && blBezirkCodes.has(r.bezirk_code) && r.repeater_is_linked);",
  "new_string": "  const domesticBlCodes = new Set(bundeslaender.filter(b => !b.is_international).map(b => b.code));\n\n  return (\n    <div className=\"space-y-2\">\n      {bundeslaender.filter(bl => !bl.is_international).map(bl => {\n        const blBezirke = bezirke.filter(b => b.bundesland_code === bl.code);\n        const defaultRepId = blRepSelection[bl.code] || 0;\n        // Match reports by bezirk's Bundesland, only for linked repeaters\n        const blBezirkCodes = new Set(blBezirke.map(b => b.code));\n        const blReports = reports.filter(r => {\n          if (!r.repeater_is_linked) return false;\n          // Primary: match by bezirk code\n          if (r.bezirk_code && blBezirkCodes.has(r.bezirk_code)) return true;\n          // Fallback for null bezirk_code: use operator BL (if domestic), else repeater BL\n          if (!r.bezirk_code) {\n            const effectiveBl = domesticBlCodes.has(r.bundesland_code) ? r.bundesland_code : r.repeater_bundesland_code;\n            return effectiveBl === bl.code;\n          }\n          return false;\n        });"
}
```

> AGENT

Deployed. Here's what was fixed:

**Problem**: BundMode filtered reports with `r.bezirk_code && blBezirkCodes.has(r.bezirk_code) && r.repeater_is_linked` — all 14 Hermannskogel reports had `bezirk_code: null`, so they were invisible.

**Fix**: 
1. **BundMode filter** now falls back to operator's Bundesland (for Austrian operators) or repeater's Bundesland (for foreign operators like DG4CK) when `bezirk_code` is null. Reports with null bezirk_code appear in the **Sonstige** row of their respective Bundesland.
2. **PATCH endpoint** now accepts `bezirk_code`, so when re-entering an operator from BundMode (UNIQUE constraint → update), the bezirk_code gets set.

The 14 Hermannskogel OE1 reports should now show in Wien's Sonstige row, and the OE3 reports under their respective NÖ bezirke.

> AGENT

I found the issues. Here's what happened:

1. **Three exercises exist for 2026-02-22**: `41f97cd2` (auto-created, OE8 repeaters: Gerlitzen, Goldeck), `81e184ee` (your first one, OE7: Rangger Köpfl), `64953840` (your re-create, OE7: Rangger Köpfl)

2. **"OE8 instead of OE7"**: You likely clicked the wrong row in the Dashboard — the pre-existing `41f97cd2` has OE8 repeaters (Gerlitzen, Goldeck). When you created your exercise, the name defaulted to just "Krisenkommunikationsübung" (no date), making it hard to distinguish from the pre-existing "Krisenkommunikationsübung 2026-02-22".

3. **"Name not changed"**: The name field on setup uses `defaultValue` + `onBlur` — if you changed the name but clicked a link/button without first clicking away from the field, the save never fired.

Two bugs to fix:

**Bug 1**: Default exercise name should include the date (so it's distinguishable).
**Bug 2**: Name field should use controlled state, not `defaultValue`.

> AGENT

Deployed. Here's the analysis and fixes:

**What happened:**
- You created exercise `81e184ee` on 2026-02-22, but a pre-existing exercise `41f97cd2` already existed for that date with OE8 repeaters (Gerlitzen, Goldeck)
- Your new exercise got the name "Krisenkommunikationsübung" (without date), while the old one was "Krisenkommunikationsübung 2026-02-22" — easy to mix up in the Dashboard
- You likely opened the old OE8 exercise by mistake, hence seeing OE8 instead of your OE7 config
- The name field used `defaultValue` + `onBlur`, so if you typed a new name but clicked a link without first clicking outside the field, the change was silently lost

**Fixes deployed:**
1. **Default name now includes date** — new exercises get "Krisenkommunikationsübung 2026-02-22" instead of just "Krisenkommunikationsübung", so multiple exercises on the same day are distinguishable
2. **Name field auto-saves** — uses controlled input with 800ms debounce + save on blur, so name changes are never lost even if you navigate away immediately

     1→# BOS-ARSA Log
     2→
     3→**Amateurfunk Notfunkübung — Live-Erfassung, Multi-User, Auswertung**
     4→
     5→A real-time, multi-user web application for BOS-ARSA amateur radio exercises across Austria. Multiple operators simultaneously log signal reports from ~100 ham radio stations on repeaters and direct frequencies. BOS-ARSA Log replaces the shared Excel workbook and standalone HTML prototypes with a single unified tool.
     6→
     7→Part of the [oeradio.at](https://oeradio.at) ecosystem.
     8→
     9→## Tech Stack
    10→
    11→| Layer | Technology |
    12→|-------|-----------|
    13→| Frontend | React 18, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Socket.IO client |
    14→| Backend | Node.js, Express, TypeScript, Socket.IO server |
    15→| Database | SQLite via better-sqlite3 |
    16→| Auth | Username/password with bcrypt + JWT tokens |
    17→| Security | Helmet, rate limiting, CORS restriction, non-root Docker |
    18→| Deployment | Docker, Docker Compose, Cloudflare Tunnel |
    19→
    20→## Architecture
    21→
    22→```
    23→/client          React SPA (Vite)
    24→/server          Express API + WebSocket server
    25→/data            SQLite database (Docker volume-mounted)
    26→```
    27→
    28→- RESTful API for CRUD operations, WebSocket (Socket.IO) for real-time sync between concurrent users
    29→- Server serves the built client in production
    30→- SQLite keeps deployment simple — the data volume is small (~1,000 operators, ~200 reports/week)
    31→
    32→## Key Domain Concepts
    33→
    34→| Concept | Description |
    35→|---------|-------------|
    36→| **Operator (Rufzeichen)** | Ham radio callsign, e.g. OE8YML, S55UJE |
    37→| **Repeater/Umsetzer** | Radio relay station with TX frequency, offset, CTCSS |
    38→| **Linked Repeater** | One logical repeater spanning multiple physical sites (Einstiegspunkte) |
    39→| **Einstiegspunkt** | Physical entry point in a linked repeater network, e.g. Hermannskogel (HK) |
    40→| **Signal Report (Rapport)** | RST format, e.g. "5/9+30 HK" = R5 / S9+30dB via Hermannskogel |
    41→| **Exercise (Übung)** | One session with configured repeaters and collected reports |
    42→| **Bezirk** | Austrian political district, identified by 2-3 letter code |
    43→| **Bundesland** | Austrian state (OE1=Wien through OE9=Vorarlberg) |
    44→| **Nachbarland** | Neighbor country (SI, CZ, DE, IT, SK, HR, LI, CH, HU) |
    45→
    46→## Features
    47→
    48→### Dashboard
    49→
    50→- **Year filter** — Button row to switch between years (2026, 2027, ...), derived from existing data
    51→- **Type filter** — Checkbox filter by exercise type (KriKom, Notfunk, etc.), appears when multiple types exist in a year
    52→- Summary cards, trend chart, and exercise table filtered by selected year and type
    53→- Exercise table shows type (short label), name, participants, and reports with quarterly subtotals
    54→
    55→### Two Data Entry Modes
    56→
    57→- **Frequenzen (Land)** — Repeater-first entry. Select a repeater, enter reports grouped by Bezirk. Each repeater card includes a "?? Sonstige" row for operators from outside the repeater's Bundesland.
    58→- **OE-Link (Bund)** — Geography-first entry. Bundesland/Bezirk hierarchy with linked repeater selection per district. Reports stay in the Bundesland where they were entered, regardless of the repeater's physical location. Each Bundesland includes a "?? Sonstige" row. Only available when OE-Link mode is enabled for the exercise. Linked repeaters are automatically added when OE-Link is toggled on and are hidden from the Frequenzen setup.
    59→
    60→### Exercise Setup
    61→
    62→- **Exercise type** selection (Krisenkommunikationsübung, 80m Notfunk Runde, or custom free-text types)
    63→- Optional exercise name (e.g. "Sonntagsrunde KW 07")
    64→- Bundesland selection grid (OE1–OE9) with one-click activation of all repeaters per state
    65→- ~80 pre-configured Austrian repeaters from OEVSV data
    66→- Custom repeater and simplex frequency creation
    67→- OE-Link toggle for linked repeater mode
    68→- Per-repeater operator (OP) callsign assignment
    69→
    70→### Interactive Austria Map with Neighbor Countries
    71→
    72→- Choropleth map of Austria (OE1–OE9) with participant/report density
    73→- 9 neighbor countries displayed: Germany, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Hungary, Slovenia, Italy, Switzerland, Liechtenstein, Croatia
    74→- High-resolution borders from Natural Earth 10m data
    75→- Countries with participating operators are color-coded by activity level
    76→- Hover tooltips showing participant count and report count per region
    77→
    78→### Automatic Callsign-to-Country Assignment
    79→
    80→- Foreign callsign prefixes automatically mapped to the correct country (e.g. S55UJE → Slovenia, DL1ABC → Germany)
    81→- Supported prefixes: OE1–OE9, S5 (Slovenia), OK/OL (Czech Republic), DA-DR (Germany), I (Italy), OM (Slovakia), 9A (Croatia), HB0 (Liechtenstein), HB (Switzerland), HA/HG (Hungary)
    82→- Strips portable/mobile suffixes (/P, /M, /OE8) before matching
    83→- Auto-derived on operator creation; existing operators backfilled via migration
    84→
    85→### Live Multi-User
    86→
    87→- Socket.IO real-time sync — reports entered by one user appear instantly for all others
    88→- Running totals bar always visible: participant count, total reports, per-repeater counts
    89→- Optimized for speed: autofocus, enter-to-submit, auto-uppercase, keyboard shortcuts
    90→- **Two-step Enter flow** — Enter in the callsign field jumps to the rapport field (cursor at end); Enter in the rapport field submits the report
    91→- Repeater headers show callsign in parentheses (e.g. "Laaerberg 2m (OE1XFW)")
    92→- OE-Link Bundesland headers with OE prefix (e.g. "OE1 Wien", "OE8 Kärnten")
    93→
    94→### Keyboard Shortcuts
    95→
    96→| Shortcut | Action |
    97→|----------|--------|
    98→| `Alt+1` through `Alt+9` | Insert "5/1" through "5/9" in rapport field |
    99→| `Ctrl+1` through `Ctrl+9` | Insert "OE1" through "OE9" in callsign field |
   100→| `Enter` (in callsign) | Jump to rapport field |
   101→| `Enter` (in rapport/notes) | Submit report and clear fields |
   102→| `Arrow Up/Down` | Navigate autocomplete suggestions |
   103→| `Escape` | Close autocomplete dropdown |
   104→
   105→### Reports & Export
   106→
   107→- **Per-exercise reports** — Summary with per-repeater and per-Bezirk/Bundesland/Land breakdown
   108→- **Auswertung (Aggregated Reports)** — Date-range aggregated statistics across multiple exercises
   109→  - Quick-select buttons: Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4, full year
   110→  - Custom date range (Von / Bis) picker
   111→  - Exercise type filter (multi-select checkboxes: KriKom, Notfunk, etc.)
   112→  - Summary cards: unique participants, total reports, exercise count, average participants per exercise
   113→  - Collapsible exercise list with per-exercise breakdown
   114→  - Deduplicates participants across exercises for accurate totals
   115→- Interactive Austria map with neighbor countries showing participant distribution
   116→- Bar chart (stations vs. reports) and pie chart (distribution by Bundesland/Land)
   117→- Participants list with callsign, name, location, report count
   118→- Export formats:
   119→  - **PNG** — Full-page screenshot of the analytics view
   120→  - **ADIF** — Amateur Data Interchange Format (.adi) for import into QRZ.com, LOTW, and other logbook software
   121→  - **TXT OE-Link** — Bundesland-grouped text export
   122→  - **TXT Frequenzen** — Repeater-grouped text export
   123→  - **TXT Kombiniert** — Summary statistics with per-repeater breakdown
   124→
   125→### Bezirk Assignment
   126→
   127→- **Operator bezirk** (home location) and **report bezirk** (where the rapport was given) are independent
   128→- Operator home bezirk is auto-derived from QTH address when possible (matching against district names)
   129→- Report bezirk is stored per signal report from the entry row context
   130→- An operator can travel and report from any bezirk without affecting their registered home location
   131→- All stats, exports, and charts group by the report's bezirk
   132→
   133→### Operator Registry
   134→
   135→- Searchable operator database (callsign, name, QTH)
   136→- Quick-add during live entry when callsign not found
   137→- Inline editing of operator details (Name, QTH) directly from report entry forms
   138→- Operator Name and QTH displayed alongside callsign in all report lists
   139→- Paginated browsing (50 per page)
   140→- Bulk import from official Fernmeldebehörde Rufzeichenliste PDF (see below)
   141→
   142→### Security
   143→
   144→- Helmet security headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options)
   145→- Rate limiting on login (10 attempts per 15 minutes)
   146→- CORS restricted to configured origin
   147→- JWT secret fail-fast in production
   148→- Request body size limit (1MB)
   149→- Input length validation
   150→- Docker container runs as non-root user
   151→- Port bound to localhost only (Cloudflare tunnel access)
   152→
   153→### User Roles
   154→
   155→| Capability | Admin | Erfasser |
   156→|-----------|-------|----------|
   157→| Create exercises | ✓ | — |
   158→| Configure repeaters | ✓ | — |
   159→| Change exercise type/name/date | ✓ | — |
   160→| Enable OE-Link | ✓ | — |
   161→| Enter/edit/delete reports | ✓ | ✓ |
   162→| Manage operators | ✓ | ✓ |
   163→| View analytics & export | ✓ | ✓ |
   164→
   165→## Getting Started
   166→
   167→### Prerequisites
   168→
   169→- Node.js 20+
   170→- npm
   171→
   172→### Development
   173→
   174→```bash
   175→# Install dependencies
   176→npm install
   177→cd server && npm install && cd ..
   178→cd client && npm install && cd ..
   179→
   180→# Seed the database with reference data (idempotent — safe to run multiple times)
   181→npm run db:seed
   182→
   183→# Start both client and server in dev mode
   184→npm run dev
   185→```
   186→
   187→The client runs on `http://localhost:5173` with API proxy to `http://localhost:3000`.
   188→
   189→### Production (Docker)
   190→
   191→```bash
   192→# Build and run
   193→docker compose up -d
   194→
   195→# Seed database (first run only — idempotent, won't overwrite existing data)
   196→docker exec bosarsalog node dist/server/db/seed.js
   197→```
   198→
   199→Required environment variables:
   200→
   201→| Variable | Description |
   202→|----------|-------------|
   203→| `JWT_SECRET` | Random 64+ char secret (required in production) |
   204→| `CORS_ORIGIN` | Allowed origin URL (default: `https://bosarsalog.oeradio.at`) |
   205→| `DATABASE_PATH` | SQLite DB path (default: `/data/bosarsalog.db`) |
   206→
   207→## API
   208→
   209→All endpoints are prefixed with `/api/v1/`. Protected routes require `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
   210→
   211→### Auth
   212→
   213→```
   214→POST /api/v1/auth/login    { username, password } -> { token, admin }
   215→```
   216→
   217→### Exercises
   218→
   219→```
   220→GET    /api/v1/exercises              List all (with summary stats)
   221→POST   /api/v1/exercises              Create { date, name, exercise_type }
   222→GET    /api/v1/exercises/:id          Full exercise with reports
   223→PATCH  /api/v1/exercises/:id          Update (name, exercise_type, organisator, oe_link)
   224→GET    /api/v1/exercises/:id/stats    Live statistics
   225→GET    /api/v1/exercises/:id/reports  All signal reports
   226→POST   /api/v1/exercises/:id/reports  Create report
   227→PATCH  /api/v1/exercises/:id/reports/:rid  Edit report
   228→DELETE /api/v1/exercises/:id/reports/:rid  Delete report
   229→```
   230→
   231→### Exercise Repeaters
   232→
   233→```
   234→GET    /api/v1/exercises/:id/repeaters
   235→POST   /api/v1/exercises/:id/repeaters      Activate repeater
   236→PATCH  /api/v1/exercises/:id/repeaters/:rid  Update OP assignment
   237→DELETE /api/v1/exercises/:id/repeaters/:rid  Deactivate repeater
   238→```
   239→
   240→### Operators
   241→
   242→```
   243→GET    /api/v1/operators         List/search (?q= for autocomplete)
   244→POST   /api/v1/operators         Quick-add new operator
   245→GET    /api/v1/operators/:id     Full profile with history
   246→PATCH  /api/v1/operators/:id     Update operator
   247→```
   248→
   249→### Reference Data
   250→
   251→```
   252→GET /api/v1/reference/bundeslaender
   253→GET /api/v1/reference/bezirke
   254→GET /api/v1/reference/einstiegspunkte
   255→GET /api/v1/repeaters
   256→GET /api/v1/repeaters/:id/einstiegspunkte
   257→```
   258→
   259→### Aggregated Reports
   260→
   261→```
   262→GET /api/v1/reports/stats?from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD[&types=...]   Aggregated stats (optional type filter)
   263→```
   264→
   265→### Export
   266→
   267→```
   268→GET /api/v1/export/exercises/:id/bund      TXT (Bundesland-grouped)
   269→GET /api/v1/export/exercises/:id/land      TXT (Repeater-grouped)
   270→GET /api/v1/export/exercises/:id/combined  Summary report
   271→```
   272→
   273→### WebSocket Events (Socket.IO)
   274→
   275→```
   276→Client -> Server:
   277→  join_exercise      { exercise_id }
   278→  leave_exercise     { exercise_id }
   279→  report_created     { report data }
   280→  report_updated     { report data }
   281→  report_deleted     { report_id }
   282→  attendance_updated { attendance data }
   283→
   284→Server -> Client (broadcast):
   285→  report_created     { report, entered_by }
   286→  report_updated     { report, entered_by }
   287→  report_deleted     { report_id, entered_by }
   288→  attendance_updated { attendance, entered_by }
   289→```
   290→
   291→## Rufzeichen Import (Fernmeldebehörde PDF)
   292→
   293→Import operators from the official Austrian Rufzeichenliste PDF published by the Fernmeldebüro:
   294→
   295→```bash
   296→# Update mode (default) — insert new, update existing name/qth
   297→RUFZEICHEN_MODE=update npm run import:rufzeichen -- /path/to/Rufzeichenliste.pdf
   298→
   299→# Skip mode — insert new only, leave existing untouched
   300→RUFZEICHEN_MODE=skip npm run import:rufzeichen -- /path/to/Rufzeichenliste.pdf
   301→```
   302→
   303→Requires `pdftotext` (poppler-utils). On NixOS: `nix-shell -p nodejs poppler-utils --run "..."`.
   304→
   305→The script parses callsign, name, and Standort (QTH) from the PDF table. Bundesland is auto-derived from the callsign prefix. Redacted entries (`*-*-*`) are skipped. The import is idempotent.
   306→
   307→## Seed Data
   308→
   309→The seed script (`npm run db:seed`) is **idempotent** — it only inserts data if the tables are empty, and never deletes existing data. It populates:
   310→
   311→- **18 Bundesländer** — 9 Austrian states + 9 international entries
   312→- **84 Bezirke** — Austrian political districts with capital flags
   313→- **~80 Repeaters** — Comprehensive OEVSV data across OE1–OE9 plus international and simplex
   314→- **12 Einstiegspunkte** — Entry points for the Magdalensberg linked system
   315→- **2 Users** — Admin and operator accounts
   316→
   317→## Conventions
   318→
   319→- German UI text, English code
   320→- Callsigns always uppercase
   321→- RST format: R/S with optional +dB modifier and location suffix
   322→- All timestamps in Europe/Vienna timezone
   323→- API prefix: `/api/v1/`
   324→- Bezirk badges: Landeshauptstadt = red, Statutarstadt/normal = gray, Sonstige (??) = yellow
   325→- Bundesland headers with blue badges
   326→- All 93 Austrian Bezirke with "C" suffix convention for Landeshauptstädte (e.g. GC=Graz, IC=Innsbruck)
   327→
   328→## License
   329→
   330→MIT

   247→          (Deutschland, Tschechien, Slowakei, Ungarn, Slowenien, Italien, Schweiz, Liechtenstein, Kroatien).
   248→          Die Farbintensität zeigt die Anzahl der Teilnehmer pro Region.
   249→          Beim Überfahren mit der Maus werden Teilnehmer- und Rapportanzahl angezeigt.
   250→        </p>
   251→        <h4 className="font-semibold text-[#1e3a5f] mt-3">Diagramme</h4>
   252→        <ul className="list-disc ml-5 space-y-1">
   253→          <li><b>Balkendiagramm</b> — Stationen und Rapporte pro Bezirk/Bundesland/Land</li>
   254→          <li><b>Kreisdiagramm</b> — Rapporte Verteilung nach Bundesland / Land</li>
   255→        </ul>
   256→        <p>
   257→          Jedes Diagramm kann einzeln als PNG-Bild heruntergeladen werden.
   258→        </p>
   259→        <h4 className="font-semibold text-[#1e3a5f] mt-3">Tabellen</h4>
   260→        <ul className="list-disc ml-5 space-y-1">
   261→          <li><b>Bezirk-Tabelle</b> — Aufschlüsselung nach Bundesland / Land und Bezirk mit Zwischensummen</li>
   262→          <li><b>Teilnehmerliste</b> — Aufklappbare Liste aller Teilnehmer mit Rufzeichen, Name, Bezirk, Bundesland / Land und Rapportanzahl</li>
   263→        </ul>
   264→        <h4 className="font-semibold text-[#1e3a5f] mt-3">Export-Formate</h4>
   265→        <div className="overflow-x-auto">
   266→          <table className="w-full text-sm border border-gray-200 mt-2">
   267→            <thead className="bg-gray-50">
   268→              <tr>
   269→                <th className="text-left px-3 py-2 border-b font-semibold">Format</th>
   270→                <th className="text-left px-3 py-2 border-b font-semibold">Beschreibung</th>
   271→              </tr>
   272→            </thead>
   273→            <tbody>
   274→              <Shortcut keys="PNG Auswertung" desc="Screenshot der gesamten Auswertungsseite" />
   275→              <Shortcut keys="ADIF (.adi)" desc="QSO-Daten für QRZ.com, LOTW und andere Logbuch-Software" />
   276→              <Shortcut keys="TXT — OE-Link" desc="Textdatei, gruppiert nach Bundesland und Bezirk" />
   277→              <Shortcut keys="TXT — Frequenzen" desc="Textdatei, gruppiert nach Umsetzer und Bezirk" />
   278→              <Shortcut keys="TXT — Kombiniert" desc="Zusammenfassung mit Statistiken und Umsetzer-Aufschlüsselung" />
   279→            </tbody>
   280→          </table>
   281→        </div>
   282→      </Section>
   283→
   284→      {/* ── Rufzeichen-Verwaltung ── */}
   285→      <Section title="7. Rufzeichen-Verwaltung">
   286→        <p>
   287→          Unter <b>Rufzeichen</b> in der Navigation finden Sie die Operator-Datenbank.
   288→        </p>
   289→        <h4 className="font-semibold text-[#1e3a5f] mt-3">Suche</h4>
   290→        <p>
   291→          Das Suchfeld durchsucht Rufzeichen, Name und QTH gleichzeitig. Die Suche startet automatisch
   292→          nach kurzer Verzögerung (300ms).
   293→        </p>
   294→        <h4 className="font-semibold text-[#1e3a5f] mt-3">Neuen Operator anlegen</h4>
   295→        <p>
   296→          Mit <b>+ Neu</b> können Sie manuell einen neuen Operator anlegen (Rufzeichen, Name, QTH, Bezirk, Bundesland).
   297→          Operatoren werden auch automatisch angelegt, wenn ein unbekanntes Rufzeichen bei der Datenerfassung eingegeben wird.
   298→        </p>
   299→        <h4 className="font-semibold text-[#1e3a5f] mt-3">Automatische Länderzuordnung</h4>
   300→        <p>
   301→          Das Bundesland bzw. Nachbarland wird automatisch anhand des Rufzeichen-Präfixes zugeordnet
   302→          (z.B. OE8 → Kärnten, S55 → Slowenien, DL → Deutschland).
   303→          Suffixe wie /P, /M oder /OE8 werden dabei ignoriert.
   304→        </p>
   305→        <h4 className="font-semibold text-[#1e3a5f] mt-3">Automatische Bezirkszuordnung</h4>
   306→        <p>
   307→          Der <b>Bezirk</b> (Heimatbezirk) wird nach Möglichkeit automatisch aus dem QTH (Standort) abgeleitet
   308→          (z.B. „Graz" → GC, „Wien" → WC, „Mödling" → MD). Wenn keine Zuordnung möglich ist,
   309→          kann der Bezirk manuell gesetzt werden.
   310→        </p>
   311→        <h4 className="font-semibold text-[#1e3a5f] mt-3">Bezirk in Rapports vs. Rufzeichenliste</h4>
   312→        <p>
   313→          Der <b>Heimatbezirk</b> eines Operators (in der Rufzeichenliste) und der <b>Rapport-Bezirk</b> (wo der Rapport
   314→          abgegeben wurde) sind unabhängig voneinander. Ein Operator kann reisen und von jedem Bezirk aus
   315→          einen Rapport abgeben, ohne dass sein Heimatbezirk verändert wird.
   316→          Auswertungen, Exporte und Diagramme gruppieren nach dem Rapport-Bezirk.
   317→        </p>
   318→        <h4 className="font-semibold text-[#1e3a5f] mt-3">Operator bearbeiten</h4>
   319→        <p>
   320→          Klicken Sie auf <b>Bearb.</b> in der Operatoren-Tabelle, um alle Felder inline zu bearbeiten.
   321→          Bestätigen Sie mit dem Häkchen oder brechen Sie mit X ab.
   322→        </p>
   323→      </Section>
   324→
   325→      {/* ── Rufzeichen-Import ── */}
   326→      <Section title="8. Rufzeichen-Import (Fernmeldebehörde)">
   327→        <p>
   328→          Rufzeichen können aus der offiziellen <b>Rufzeichenliste der Fernmeldebehörde</b> (PDF) automatisch
   329→          importiert werden. Das Skript liest die PDF-Datei, extrahiert Rufzeichen, Name und Standort (QTH)
   330→          und aktualisiert die Operator-Datenbank.
   331→        </p>
   332→        <h4 className="font-semibold text-[#1e3a5f] mt-3">Importmodus</h4>
   333→        <ul className="list-disc ml-5 space-y-1">
   334→          <li><b>RUFZEICHEN_MODE=update</b> — Neue Rufzeichen einfügen, bestehende mit Name/QTH aktualisieren (Standard)</li>
   335→          <li><b>RUFZEICHEN_MODE=skip</b> — Nur neue Rufzeichen einfügen, bestehende nicht verändern</li>
   336→        </ul>
   337→        <h4 className="font-semibold text-[#1e3a5f] mt-3">Ausführung</h4>
   338→        <p>
   339→          Das Bundesland wird automatisch aus dem Rufzeichen-Präfix abgeleitet (OE1 = Wien, OE8 = Kärnten, usw.).
   340→          Gesperrte Rufzeichen (<code>*-*-*</code>) werden übersprungen.
   341→          Der Import ist idempotent — bei unverändertem Datenbestand werden keine Änderungen vorgenommen.
   342→        </p>
   343→        <p>
   344→          Voraussetzung: <code>pdftotext</code> (poppler-utils) muss installiert sein.
   345→        </p>
   346→      </Section>
   347→
   348→      {/* ── Rollen ── */}
   349→      <Section title="9. Benutzerrollen">
   350→        <div className="overflow-x-auto">
   351→          <table className="w-full text-sm border border-gray-200 mt-2">
   352→            <thead className="bg-gray-50">
   353→              <tr>
   354→                <th className="text-left px-3 py-2 border-b font-semibold">Funktion</th>
   355→                <th className="text-center px-3 py-2 border-b font-semibold">Admin</th>
   356→                <th className="text-center px-3 py-2 border-b font-semibold">Erfasser</th>
   357→              </tr>
   358→            </thead>
   359→            <tbody className="divide-y divide-gray-100">
   360→              <RoleRow label="Übung erstellen" admin operator={false} />
   361→              <RoleRow label="Übungstyp/Name/Datum ändern" admin operator={false} />
   362→              <RoleRow label="Umsetzer konfigurieren" admin operator={false} />
   363→              <RoleRow label="OE-Link aktivieren" admin operator={false} />
   364→              <RoleRow label="Bundesländer aktivieren" admin operator={false} />
   365→              <RoleRow label="Rapporte erfassen" admin operator />
   366→              <RoleRow label="Rapporte bearbeiten/löschen" admin operator />
   367→              <RoleRow label="Operatoren verwalten" admin operator />
   368→              <RoleRow label="Auswertung ansehen" admin operator />
   369→              <RoleRow label="Daten exportieren" admin operator />
   370→            </tbody>
   371→          </table>
   372→        </div>
   373→      </Section>
   374→
   375→      {/* ── Tipps ── */}
   376→      <Section title="10. Tipps für die Praxis">
   377→        <ul className="list-disc ml-5 space-y-2">
   378→          <li>
   379→            <b>Vor der Übung:</b> Admin erstellt die Übung, wählt die Bundesländer und aktiviert die benötigten Umsetzer.
   380→            OP-Rufzeichen pro Umsetzer eintragen.
   381→          </li>
   382→          <li>
   383→            <b>Während der Übung:</b> Alle Erfasser melden sich an und öffnen die Übung.
   384→            Rapporte werden live synchronisiert — jeder sieht sofort, was die anderen eingeben.
   385→          </li>
   386→          <li>
   387→            <b>Schnelle Eingabe:</b> Nutzen Sie Alt+1-9 für schnelle RST-Eingabe und Strg+1-9 für OE-Präfixe.
   388→            Enter im Rufzeichen-Feld springt zum RST-Feld, Enter im RST-Feld sendet den Rapport ab und springt zurück zum Rufzeichen.
   389→          </li>
   390→          <li>
   391→            <b>Unbekannte Rufzeichen:</b> Wenn ein Rufzeichen nicht in der Datenbank ist, wird es beim Speichern
   392→            automatisch als neuer Operator angelegt.
   393→          </li>
   394→          <li>
   395→            <b>Nach der Übung:</b> Auf der Auswertungsseite können Diagramme und Textdateien exportiert werden.
   396→          </li>
   397→        </ul>
   398→      </Section>
   399→
   400→      <div className="text-xs text-gray-400 pt-4 border-t">
   401→        BOS-ARSA Log &mdash; Im Sinne der Sicherheit
   402→      </div>
   403→    </div>
   404→  );
   405→}
   406→
   407→function Section({ title, children }: { title: string; children: React.ReactNode }) {
   408→  return (
   409→    <section className="space-y-2">
   410→      <h2 className="text-base font-bold text-[#1e3a5f] border-b border-gray-200 pb-1">{title}</h2>
   411→      <div className="text-sm text-gray-700 space-y-2">{children}</div>
   412→    </section>
   413→  );
   414→}
   415→
   416→function Shortcut({ keys, desc }: { keys: string; desc: string }) {
   417→  return (
   418→    <tr className="border-b border-gray-100">
   419→      <td className="px-3 py-1.5 font-mono text-xs whitespace-nowrap">{keys}</td>
   420→      <td className="px-3 py-1.5">{desc}</td>
   421→    </tr>
   422→  );
   423→}
   424→
   425→function RoleRow({ label, admin, operator }: { label: string; admin: boolean; operator: boolean }) {
   426→  return (
   427→    <tr>
   428→      <td className="px-3 py-1.5">{label}</td>
   429→      <td className="px-3 py-1.5 text-center">{admin ? '✓' : '—'}</td>
   430→      <td className="px-3 py-1.5 text-center">{operator ? '✓' : '—'}</td>
   431→    </tr>
   432→  );
   433→}
